channel.title: DE magazine Deutschland - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from DE magazine Deutschland (deutschland.de)

item.title: “Germans are like coconuts”
item.description: Hard shell, soft core: how Brittany from the United States and Abdullah from Pakistan experience the German culture of arguing

item.title: Drone defence and bomb disposal: counter-terrorism exercise in Schleswig-Holstein
item.description: How do emergency services in Germany prepare for threat scenarios? The Getex counter-terrorism exercise brings together police forces, the Federal Police and the Bundeswehr - from shooting down drones to defusing bombs.

item.title: Help for Ukrainian war victims: new mobility thanks to prostheses
item.description: They are forging new paths despite severe injuries: how a German company and its Ukrainian partners are responding to the horrors of war.

item.title: Leipzig Book Fair: Huge crowds at the opening
item.description: The Leipzig Book Fair is now open – and visitors are flocking to the halls in large numbers. Due to the high turnout on Saturday, the fair has already stopped selling day tickets.

item.title: Pistorius visits partners in the Indo-Pacific.
item.description: During talks in Japan, Singapore and Australia, discussions are expected to include strengthening their strategic dialogue.

item.title: New trade agreement: EU and Australia aim to reduce dependencies
item.description: US President Trump is alienating allies with tariffs, whilst the EU is committed to free trade and closer ties with its partners. It also intends to cooperate much more closely with Australia.

item.title: There’s no such thing as the “typical German” - or is there?
item.description: Intercultural coach Mala Ullal hears on a daily basis about how international skilled professionals experience misunderstandings in their work. What comes as a surprise to many, and what really matters.

item.title: Germany debates rape law to tackle AI and online abuse
item.description: Calls are growing for Germany to update its rape law after a celebrity case involving "deepfakes" caused an uproar. Campaigners are also pushing for a move to the "only yes means yes" principle of active consent.

item.title: How the government plans to help victims
item.description: Digital violence: What measures does the German government plan to introduce, and when, to better protect victims of digital violence? The Federal Ministry of Justice has been working on a corresponding amendment to the law to better protect victims.

item.title: German holidays: even relaxation is organised
item.description: Can Germans relax on holiday? Absolutely! In efficient, weatherproof style – and with a tightly scheduled daily plan.

item.title: More than clothing: the meaning of traditional dress
item.description: Cultural studies expert Simone Egger explains why traditional dress is far more than just a cliché in Germany and why it is again giving young people a sense of identity.

item.title: German precision: a cliché that’s true
item.description: From workbench to microchip: German precision isn’t a myth, it’s a principle - and one that has evolved historically, proven its technical worth and is still practised to this day.

item.title: Rapprochement with the West: Steinmeier receives Syrian President al-Shar
item.description: 🇸🇾 The visit was postponed in January due to an outbreak of violence in Syria. 🛬 Now, Syrian interim President al-Sharaa is making up for the missed visit to Berlin. His first stop is Bellevue Palace.

item.title: Germany pledges aid to Syria for reconstruction
item.description: 🛬 Syrian interim President al-Scharaa is visiting Germany. 💬 A key issue: the return of Syrian refugees to their homeland.

item.title: Easter bunnies and colourful eggs: where the Easter traditions originate
item.description: Easter is the most important Christian festival. Find out more about how it is celebrated these days in Germany.
